Concepts: Gattermann–Koch reaction, Friedel–Crafts acylation, Claisen–Schmidt (crossed aldol) condensation.
Step 1 (x, Gattermann–Koch): $\mathrm{C_6H_6 + CO + HCl \xrightarrow{AlCl_3/CuCl} C_6H_5CHO}$, so x = benzaldehyde.
Step 2 (y, Friedel–Crafts acylation): $\mathrm{C_6H_6 + CH_3COCl \xrightarrow{AlCl_3} C_6H_5COCH_3}$, so y = acetophenone.
Step 3 (z, Claisen–Schmidt): benzaldehyde has no α‑H. The acetophenone enolate attacks the C=O of benzaldehyde, and heating removes water.
$$\mathrm{C_6H_5CHO + CH_3COC_6H_5 \xrightarrow{OH^-,\ \Delta} C_6H_5CH{=}CH{-}CO{-}C_6H_5 + H_2O}$$
z = benzylideneacetophenone (chalcone).
Step 4 (π bonds in z): two benzene rings give $2\times3 = 6$, C=C gives 1 and C=O gives 1, for a total of 8 π bonds.
Step 5 (π electrons): $8 \times 2 = 16$.
Answer: 16
